title: Operational Group Assessment / LAST CALL
summary: Operational and behavioural assessment of the independent group known as Last Call.
body:
SUBJECT

LAST CALL

Current designation for a small independent group operating primarily within Free-Void territory.

The group was separated and detained following an incident in late August, 323 SE. Members were subsequently imprisoned at separate facilities. They were released at different points during 325 and 326 SE and did not fully reassemble until 333 SE, approximately ten years after their separation.

Available records indicate that the members had limited interaction during the intervening period despite being held apart. The nature and frequency of this contact remains unclear.

No formal organisation, corporate registration, House affiliation or recognised military command structure has been identified. The group nevertheless demonstrates a degree of internal cohesion inconsistent with its apparent history.

SOURCE LIMITATIONS

This record is assembled from surveillance, recovered documentation, institutional records, intercepted communications and indirect reporting.

Ishida, Lorenzo is considered an indirect source only. He is not affiliated with Brightside and is not believed to be aware of Brightside observation. Information attributed to Ishida has been retained where independently corroborated.

INDIVIDUAL ASSESSMENTS

KENJI

Origin: Monument. City of Luoyang.
Guardian: Saigyou Norisuke.

Kenji is an orphan originating from the Chinese colony of Luoyang. He spent his childhood in the Qing Lantern Orphanage before, in his early teens, being brought into the wider fold of Saigyou Norisuke's organisation. His direct interaction with Norisuke appears to have been limited. Most of Kenji's training was conducted within the wider organisation controlled or influenced by Norisuke.

His natural aptitude for security and combat was noted early. Available assessments indicate an innate level of skill beyond what his formal training would reasonably account for.

Outside violent encounters, Kenji presents as an ordinary individual. There is little evidence that he seeks violence for its own sake. During active conflict this changes considerably.

Kenji has a notably low threshold for deciding that a confrontation should end permanently. Once committed to violence, he acts rapidly and with little apparent hesitation. Encounters involving Kenji have a disproportionately high likelihood of ending in death.

Assessment: Kenji is not believed to seek violence. He is, however, exceptionally willing to conclude it.

KALLISTA

Origin: Globe II, designation Terath.
Source confirmation: Vulcan Research Authority documentation.

Kallista is not believed to be native to this world. In the overwhelming majority of available accounts concerning her arrival, she simply appeared. No reliable record of a conventional arrival, transport or immigration event has been located. VRA documentation is the strongest surviving source connecting her to Globe II and the designation Terath.

Kallista is frequently quiet and can appear apathetic to circumstances that would normally produce a stronger emotional response. This should not be interpreted as a lack of awareness.

She is highly attentive to language. She notices specific wording, omissions and subtle changes in phrasing that other members of the group frequently overlook. She is often more interested in exactly what someone said than in what they appear to have meant.

Kallista is proficient in Resonance, commonly referred to as magic. Her understanding extends beyond practical use. Recovered observations indicate a deep familiarity with mysticism and with the traditions, theories and concepts surrounding Resonance. The depth of this knowledge is not consistent with her known background.

Assessment: Kallista's apparent passivity should not be mistaken for inattentiveness. She listens closely, chooses her words carefully and possesses an unusually deep understanding of Resonance and mysticism.

RUBY

Surname: Unknown.
Origin: Probable Stwyx.
Current identity: Equin citizen, presumed constructed.

Ruby's documented identity is believed to be false. Available evidence suggests an origin on Stwyx, an analogue world not intended for ordinary travel or civilian departure. Her present Equin identity is assessed as fabricated or substantially altered.

Ruby possesses advanced academic qualifications in engineering, computer science and propulsion science, with exceptionally high marks. Her academic record indicates genuine expertise rather than merely adequate formal qualification.

Ruby is confident to the point of abrasiveness. She is outspoken, frequently profane and has a tendency to present herself as the most qualified person in the room even when the available evidence does not support that conclusion. This behaviour appears partly defensive.

Her actual weakness is not modern technical competence but older standardised technology. Ruby's education appears to have prioritised advanced systems while leaving substantial gaps in technologies and conventions that would have been considered common knowledge several decades earlier. She can understand extremely sophisticated systems while occasionally failing to recognise comparatively basic legacy technology.

Ruby has a documented history of stimulant dependency. Current records indicate that she is no longer using drugs. The previous dependency remains relevant as a potential historical vulnerability, but there is no current evidence of active use.

Assessment: Ruby's technical competence is genuine. Her confidence often exceeds her own private assessment of that competence. Her knowledge is unusually deep and unusually uneven.

ZEPHYR

Model classification: Legacy clanker.
Probable manufacturer: Lexxir Guild.

Zephyr was initially assessed as an unremarkable legacy artificial individual. Earlier records contain little of operational interest.

This assessment changed following the discovery of an internal Lexxir division responsible for his model line. The division is directed by Hephaestus Rigel, with Novacliss identified as a subordinate researcher.

Zephyr was located on Ruby's home world by Ruby herself. She subsequently restored him to operation. Available evidence indicates that their relationship began there and that they have continued to function largely as a duo within the wider group.

Zephyr was not created with artificial sapience. During an extended period in which he was offline, artificial sapience was granted or otherwise introduced to artificial life on a wider societal level. When Zephyr later returned to operation, he discovered that he had become a sapient individual without having experienced the process by which that change occurred.

The implications remain poorly understood. Zephyr possesses a strong and unusually consistent concept of moral justice. His understanding of personhood appears to be shaped by the fact that he became a recognised artificial person while unconscious and returned to a society that had changed without him.

Zephyr is extremely dangerous in direct conflict. His violence is deliberate rather than uncontrolled.

A particular behavioural priority has been repeatedly observed: Zephyr will defend Ruby against perceived threats, insults or coercion. The intensity of this response appears disproportionate to the immediate threat.

Assessment: Zephyr should not be treated as a passive machine or obsolete security platform. He is an artificial person with a profound discontinuity in his own history. His relationship with Ruby appears to be one of the most stable elements of his current identity.

LUCY MAYER

Original designation: LY-7-7.
Programme: Lyrix.
Origin: Apex.

Lucy Mayer was originally designated LY-7-7 and produced as part of the Lyrix programme on Apex. The programme involved genetically modified human subjects intended for piloting through the Echo and for specialised military and black-operations deployment.

Lucy was not exposed to ordinary civilian life during her early development. Records indicate that she was approximately twelve to fourteen years old when she was removed from an Apex site during an attack by an individual identified as Conner Mayer. She subsequently became Lucy Mayer.

Lucy displays significant emotional immaturity in some circumstances. She is highly curious and demonstrates a persistent interest in experiences outside the narrow environment in which she was raised.

She is also somewhat dependent on low-tier stimulants. The behaviour appears partly recreational and partly functional.

The combination of military conditioning, restricted childhood development and sudden exposure to ordinary society produces behaviour that is difficult to classify using conventional models.

Assessment: Lucy's curiosity should not be mistaken for naivety. She has been trained to operate in environments where hesitation is dangerous. Her difficulty lies elsewhere: she is still learning what ordinary people consider worth hesitating over.

GROUP PSYCHOLOGY

The group does not appear to possess a permanent leader. Authority is situational. Individual members assume control according to circumstance, after which the others generally accept the decision without prolonged dispute.

Despite approximately ten years of separation, the group resumed functioning together with comparatively little apparent difficulty in 333 SE. The limited interactions recorded during their separation may account for part of this continuity, although the available evidence is insufficient to establish how much contact occurred.

Disagreements are usually short. Group cohesion appears to increase when circumstances deteriorate.

OBSCURA'S SCAR

Shortly before their separation and subsequent incarceration, all known members of Last Call acquired an identical anomalous physical brand known as Obscura's Scar.

The origin, mechanism and purpose of the brand remain unknown. Comparable individuals bearing the same mark have reportedly demonstrated anomalous abilities. On that basis, Last Call is provisionally assessed as having acquired unknown additional capabilities.

No reliable assessment of those capabilities has yet been completed.

See restricted record ARC-326-0431.

INTERNAL NOTE

They are considerably more interesting than the original assessment suggested.

Source: Brightside internal review.
